stories.title: US hits Iran as Gulf states targeted in Hormuz flareup
stories.summary: The United States struck Iran today for a second day running, drawing Tehran's reprisals against US allies in the Gulf as the foes battle over the status of the strategic Strait of Hormuz. The fresh fighting and Iran's announcement over the weekend of a new closure of Hormuz - a key conduit in the world's oil trade - sent crude prices climbing and further battered an interim peace deal. Iran responded to the latest US attacks by targeting Gulf nations, with the powerful Revolutionary Guards announcing new strikes on Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait, according to state media reports. The US Central Command (CENTCOMM) said its forces had completed their latest barrage, which began overnight yesterday, on dozens of Iranian targets.

stories.title: Good weather 'just keeps on coming' - Met Éireann
stories.summary: The current hot temperatures are set to continue, with Meteorologist Rebecca Cantwell saying "the good weather just keeps on coming, high pressure is sticking around right through this week". A high temperature warning comes into effect for five counties today, but there is also a weather advisory for warm weather across the country. Cork, Kerry, Limerick, Galway and Mayo are covered by the Status Yellow high temperature warning that comes into effect at 1pm today and lasts until 7am Wednesday. Those counties could see maximum temperatures in excess of 27C, as well as overnight minimum temperatures in excess of 15C.

stories.title: Jurassic Park star Sam Neill dies aged 78
stories.summary: Actor Sam Neill, 78, best known for his roles in the Jurassic Park movies and TV series Peaky Blinders has died, his family has said. The Northern Ireland-born New Zealand actor, best known for playing Dr Alan Grant in the blockbuster dinosaur franchise, died in Sydney, Australia, on Monday. A statement posted to Instagram read: "It is with immense sadness that the whānau (family) of Sam Neill share the news of his passing on Monday 13th July, in Sydney Australia." "Sam was surrounded by family and passed with the dignity that has characterised his whole life."

stories.title: Drug cases in District Court up 8% year on year - report
stories.summary: Drug cases in the District Court have increased by 8% year on year, according to the annual report of the Courts Service, which was published today. The chairperson of the board of the Courts Service, Justice Aileen Donnelly, said that the rise in drug cases of a less serious kind had increased the workload of the lower courts. There were 30,018 new drug cases before the District Court last year, compared to 27,783 in 2024. Public order and assault cases also showed an increase of 11 per year over two years, according to the 2025 annual report.

stories.title: Fire exits in Bangkok bar were impeded, says governor
stories.summary: An explosive fire at a pub in Thailand's capital Bangkok killed 27 people and injured dozens more yesterday, officials said, after obstructed emergency exits hindered patrons choking on smoke from escaping the burning venue. "There are two fire exits, one is near the kitchen. There were beer crates in the way," Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt told reporters, adding that there was a table in the way of the other fire exit, hindering evacuation. "We need to wait for forensic investigators to examine the scene more closely," he added. One video of the incident posted on social media and verified by Reuters showed thick smoke billowing out of the pub, before an intense horizontal plume of fire jets out of a doorway, as screaming customers fled the premises around midnight local time.

stories.title: CAB handed €15m over to exchequer from seizures in 2025
stories.summary: The Criminal Assets Bureau handed over almost €15m to the exchequer last year from asset seizures, auctions and proceeds of crime actions, according to its annual report. The luxury homes include the Co Leitrim bungalow belonging to Kinahan gang drug dealer Niall Smith and the lavishly renovated Dublin city home of the rival Hutch gang member James 'Mago' Gately. CAB also sold the home of Eduard Chiper, who it described as the leader of a transnational organised crime group consisting of Moldovans living in Ireland, Moldova and Spain. CAB’s latest annual report for 2025 shows it returned over €14.9m to the exchequer.
